Google now writes the review line in your UK search ad. Under the CAP Code, you answer for it.

Google now writes positive-only summaries of online reviews into UK Search ads, and you can't edit them. In this clip Hannah and I ask who is responsible for a line Google wrote. Under the CAP Code it's the marketer, and the ASA hasn't ruled on anything like this yet.

The job to hand AI this week is reading your reviews the way Google will. Give it six months of reviews from the sites that rank for your brand name, and it hands back the positive themes most likely to appear in a summary, each marked for whether you'd be comfortable claiming it in an ad.

The voices on the podcast are AI-generated.

Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/google-ads-ai-review-summaries-uk/
clips.text: Who's responsible for a line Google wrote? The CAP Code, the rulebook the Advertising Standards Authority enforces, says primary responsibility sits with the marketer. And rule three point four six covers consumer reviews directly. You mustn't publish them, or information derived from them, in a misleading way, and the Code's own examples include showing the positive ones while leaving out the negative ones. And a positive-only summary is, by definition, the positive ones. That's the question. The ASA hasn't ruled on anything like this, so nobody can tell you the answer yet.
